does: Cooks skewered minced meat over glowing coals, turning it often, so that the outside takes a smoky crust while the inside stays juicy.

intro.what: This method grills skewered minced meat over glowing coals, turning it often for a smoky crust.
intro.why: It teaches you to manage coals, turning and flare-ups instead of exposing the skewers to tall flames.

how: Let the coals burn down until they are covered in grey ash and glow evenly, with no tall flame.
Lay the skewers across the coals, close enough to sizzle at once.
Turn the skewers often, so that they colour on every side and no side burns.
Fan the coals if they fade, and move the skewers aside if fat drips and flares.
Take the skewers off when they are browned all over and the meat feels firm.

cues.text: The meat is browned and speckled with dark spots on every side, with no black patch.
A smoky, meaty scent rises from the coals.
The meat springs back when pressed, instead of giving way.

mistakes.mistake: Grilling over open flame, which blackens the outside before the middle is ready.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the coals glow under grey ash.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the skewers in one place, so that one side burns.
Pressing the meat flat on the grate, which squeezes out the juice.

quiz.question: Why wait for glowing coals rather than tall flames?
choices: To keep the surface from browning.
To develop a smoky crust without blackening the outside too quickly.
To let flames touch every side continuously.
quiz.because: Open flame blackens the outside too quickly; evenly glowing coals provide the intended grilling heat.

quiz.question: How should you turn these skewers?
choices: Only after the first side blackens.
Keep the same side facing the coals throughout.
quiz.because: Frequent turning distributes the browning instead of letting a single side burn.

quiz.question: What appearance is the aim on the meat?
choices: Browning and dark speckles without black patches.
A pale surface with no colour.
A black crust on the side facing the coals.
quiz.because: The intended crust is browned and speckled, rather than burnt black.

quiz.question: Dripping fat causes a flare-up below the skewers. What would you do?
choices: Hold them closer to the flames.
Press the meat down onto the grate.
quiz.because: Moving skewers aside keeps a flare from blackening their surface.

comes_after.why: The meat has to be held on a skewer before it can be turned over the coals.

variant_of.differs: Grilling cooks close to a fierce, direct heat, often from above. Here the heat is glowing charcoal underneath, the food lies across the coals on skewers, and it is turned constantly.
